records.c: Install the shared IRQ and audio, select five stage pointers, clear the local section and initialise screen, scrolling and sprite slots.
Apply the section-specific timer and camera configuration and clear the completion and scrolling fields before redrawing.
Update the lives display and start the tune indexed by the section when the current value differs.
Latch the active-low joystick byte, wait for the sprite IRQ and perform shared player and action processing. A set flag at $25DE selects a redraw without advancing the stage counter.
Scan placements, update active slots, poll weapon and pause controls, tick the timer and redraw. Check the completion and death states before returning to the input poll.
Request an effect and wait, then advance the local section. After two sections this path displays the completion banner and loads D.
Align the start column to a 64-column boundary, reset transient state and decrement the life count.
Run the game-over and high-score routines, then wait for fire and test the available continuation. A continuation resets the score and lives.
Show the round-6-cleared banner and transfer to the disk loader for D.
Two tune numbers indexed by the local section in load C.
Jump through the pointer at $2917 plus twice the local section index.
Pair of little-endian addresses of load C's round setup routines.
High byte of the first round setup address, indexed by the even section offset.
Clear the column state and initialise the timer. Set the map origin to row $EC and select the 96-byte stride with $277E=$60.
Draw the round-5-cleared banner before configuring the next section.
Dispatch through the two little-endian palette pointers selected by $3D63.
Two palette initialisers selected by the current round number.
High byte of the first palette handler pointer, indexed by the same even offset.
Set the first round’s background colours and use the 19-row palette at $3AB0.
Set the second round’s background colours and use $3AC3 for its row palette.
Draw the score panel and copy the 34-glyph restart message into the screen at $FA33.
The 34 glyphs of REWIND TAPE TO 0000 THEN PRESS PLAY, displayed when the game needs a restart.
Reset the four upgrade flags and icon pointers and clear the shadow count.
Latch a fresh Space press and cycle the even weapon index. Clear current projectiles and refresh the view through the active map-stride path before installing the new callbacks.
Use the local section and camera coordinates to select placement callbacks. Allow the lower row margin to wrap near row 255 and clear out-of-range work flags.
Starting placement index for each of this load’s 2 sections. The scanner walks backward.
The scanner stops once its decremented placement index equals this section’s stop value.
Low bytes of the map columns compared with the current viewport column.
High bytes of those columns, compared with the active map page before checking X and Y.
Map row for each placement. The scanner tests it against the current row and its lower margin.
Work flags for each placement. The scanner clears the corresponding byte when its placement leaves the active viewport.
Map placement callbacks for this load. The scanner at $2A53 selects one of 18 pointers and jumps to it via $14.
High byte of the first interleaved position-specific handler pointer.
Single return byte before the placement handlers.
Call three local placement helpers and then enter the common continuation at $2D56.
Run the overlapping placement helpers, reload the current record index and enter a different continuation at $2DDB.
Check the one-in-64 random gate and free slot. Choose a random X, start near the bottom of the playfield and give the actor an upward velocity.
Update the placement state, test the 64-tick phase and allocate a free slot with coordinates chosen from the random generator.
Capture the current map origin as both camera limits and zero fine vertical scroll. Update the playfield colour and count placement passes before starting the encounter.
Copy 14 rows of 17 tile bytes from the map at $41EF to screen RAM at $F833, advancing source and destination by their respective row strides.
Allocate a type-$1B actor on the selected stage phase and initialise its position, sprite pointer, colour and work bytes.
Allow the spawn when fewer than two relevant objects are active and the 64-tick phase matches. Allocate a slot, choose two random coordinates and select its initial state.
On the 128-tick phase offset by $3F, allocate a slot at the placement row and set type $10 and screen X=$AA.
Use the 128-tick phase, a random Y coordinate and its low bit to choose one of two horizontal starts and velocities.
Pair of horizontal starting positions selected by the random low bit.
Pair of horizontal velocities for the left and right starts respectively.
Use the 64-tick phase to allocate a free sprite. Test the random lane index and apply its position, shape and velocities.
Four starting X positions for the object created at the top of the viewport.
Horizontal velocities for those four launch lanes.
Vertical velocities chosen with the same lane index.
Initial sprite pointers for the four lanes.
Set the placement-active flag, lock the map column and start tune 2. Save the player X coordinate when the encounter-active byte is clear.
Reserve four slots, retain their IDs and arrange them around the saved player X coordinate using the component offset and sprite pointer tables.
Four object types selected by the encounter setup at $2DEC.
Check the spawn phase and free slot, translate placement coordinates and start the object with type 5 and a cleared hit state.
Rounds the running type-5 and type-9 spawn count into an eight-state cycle for the alternate colour.
Use the placement’s low column byte and camera origin to calculate the initial horizontal coordinate.
Subtract the camera’s row, convert to pixels and add the playfield top and fine vertical scroll.
Scan active logical slots and select each slot’s type handler. Subtract the camera movement from object coordinates and check the new position against the viewport limits before dispatch.
Jump through the object or placement callback in $14.
31 little-endian pointer entries indexed by twice the active slot type at $8E,X. The update pass at $2EBF skips a zero type before fetching its pointer.
High bytes of the object handler list, indexed by twice the slot’s type.
Left-side extent used by the collision rectangle code at $1740.
Per-type flag gating the collision callback in the shared pass at $1586.
Top-side extent read by $1740 when constructing an object’s tile rectangle.
Bottom-side extent read by $1740 to bound the vertical overlap test.
Check player contact after the slot reaches phase five. On the scheduled tick at phase six, reserve three component slots for its next phase.
Initial animation frame sequence indexed by the phase stored in the actor’s slot.
Three extra shape values adjacent to the type-$0D animation frames.
Ignore the creation tick, then advance the shape by four on eighth ticks. Remove the object when it reaches shape $AA.
Integrate two velocity steps every fourth tick. If hit, transform the object into effect type $0B before checking player overlap.
A slot state of $FF enters the intermittent defeat sound and effects, with a thirty-count limit. Other states follow the live path.
Eight columns added to the viewport row address for the encounter’s tile effects.
Eight row indices used to locate the corresponding screen addresses.
Eight horizontal coordinates for encounter effect sprites.
Eight vertical coordinates paired with the encounter effect X table.
Award one score unit on a registered hit and switch to the common flash effect.
Three horizontal velocities for the fragments spawned during the encounter.
Three vertical steps paired with the fragment X velocities.
Initial pointers for the three fragment slots.
Shape pointers for the type-$11 slot’s animation phase.
Award two score units, start the shared visual effect, set its resulting type to $19 and queue sound $0A.
Extra return instruction between the slot update routines.
Apply hit colour and cooldown, clearing the flag so each registered hit increases the count once.
Clear the activity of the slot indexed by $9D,X and move its Y out of view.
Update the hit tally and cooldown for a different encounter body slot, starting from its normal colour.
Mark the encounter active and choose a movement or encounter phase according to the slot timer.
Four frame pointers for the left step, also used as the initial display group.
Four pointers for the second leftward phase.
Four shape pointers restored when the actor settles.
Four pointers paired with the rightward component movement.
Second rightward group of four shape pointers.
Four component shapes for the later encounter phase.
After the delay reaches 20, sample the map above the object and test player overlap when the tile and hit state permit.
Convert the hit object into effect type $0B, queue effect $0E and award one score unit.
Advance the shared pickup animation and periodically try to launch a particle at random offsets.
Increment the stage and per-slot timers. Advance the shape every eight local ticks before entering the next phase at $6A.
Eight pointers indexed by the entering actor’s phase.
Nine horizontal velocities applied to newly spawned objects.
Nine corresponding vertical velocities for those objects.
Flash on a registered hit, clear the flag and start the cooldown. On the third hit, run the shared replacement effect and switch to type $19.
On a hit, increase the score and choose a response according to the object’s normal or alternate colour.
Repeat the selected colour in all 40 cells of each of 19 playfield rows.
Nineteen row colours read from the first round’s palette setup.
Nineteen row colours read from the second round’s palette setup.
The third set of nineteen row colour bytes, with colour 9 after the first row’s colour 15.
The attribute byte returned by the shared map query at $127B for the tile read from the stage map.
Select the shared 512-byte map patcher when $277E is zero. Otherwise compute the 96-byte row address and patch all 19 copy operands inside $222A.
